explanation: France doesn't treat the head as sacred the way some Southeast and South Asian cultures do, so there's no religious or spiritual taboo against touching it. Still, French physical contact is generally reserved for people you already know well, so patting an adult's head — especially a stranger's — would read as condescending or overly familiar, even though it's common and affectionate with young children.
local_tip: Avoid touching an adult's head; a hand on the shoulder or arm is the more normal, lower-risk way to show warmth among people who already know each other.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body; touching anyone's head, adult or child, is a serious taboo.
Patting a child's head can be affectionate, but touching an adult's head is generally avoided out of respect, especially in Hindu contexts.
Patting someone's head can come across as playful or condescending depending on context; it's best reserved for close friends or children.
